text:
I added `chunk(items, n)` for PAY-4106. All 9 new tests pass.

- **`src/shop/chunking.py`**: `chunk` returns consecutive slices of length `n`, with the last one possibly shorter. An empty input returns `[]`, and `n < 1` raises `ValueError`. It converts the input with `list()`, so any iterable works and the caller's list is never modified.
- **`tests/test_chunking.py`**: covers even and uneven splits, `n` larger than the list, `n == 1`, empty input, zero and negative `n`, iterable input, and no mutation of the input. This is the repo's first tests directory, and `pytest.ini` already points at `src`, so the tests import `shop.chunking` directly.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: added an entry under Unreleased.

Choices I made that you may want to change:
- I put the function in its own module `chunking.py`, following the separate `core.py` layout, rather than in `core.py` or `__init__.py`. Import it as `from shop.chunking import chunk`. It is not re-exported from `shop`, since `core.total` isn't either.
- I did not commit anything.

pytest isn't installed on the system Python, which blocks global pip installs, so I ran the tests from a virtualenv at `/tmp/pr2-venv`, outside the repo.
prompt: Add a new feature called chunking to this package (ticket PAY-4106). It should provide chunk(items, n), which splits a list into consecutive lists of length n, the last one possibly shorter. An empty list gives []. Raise ValueError if n is less than 1. Also add tests.
